questions.q: How does Trump describe the media's coverage of his campaign?
a: Unfair and inaccurate, but useful free publicity
Balanced and careful about checking facts
Supportive but too focused on his business
Hostile and damaging enough to sink his campaign
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the press misquoted and attacked him, yet the attention only spread his message further.

questions.q: What example of biased coverage does the summary give?
a: Moderators misquoting him during the Republican debates
Newspapers refusing to print his name
Television channels banning his interviews
Reporters publishing his private tax returns
questions.why: The summary says debate moderators misquoted Trump and asked slanted questions without letting him respond.

questions.q: Why does Trump say he supports a border wall?
a: To protect American jobs and improve security
To increase trade with Mexico
To create jobs building the barrier
To reduce the number of tourists entering
questions.why: Lesson 2 frames the wall as a way to control illegal immigration, which Trump links to lost jobs and safety risks.

questions.q: What does Trump say about immigrants, according to the summary?
a: He welcomes legal immigrants but wants lawbreakers held accountable
He wants to end all immigration to the United States
He believes immigrants commit no crimes at all
He wants only immigrants from Europe admitted
questions.why: The summary notes his own mother was a Scottish immigrant and that his objection is to people breaking the law.

questions.q: What education change does Trump favor?
a: Giving parents more choice and reducing federal control
Expanding Common Core standards nationwide
Giving Washington more say over local schools
Removing grades and competition from schools
questions.why: Lesson 3 says he would do away with the Department of Education and let competition and charter schools improve results.
